findings.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, so deleting a client (and roles/groups via the same listener path) will throw and abort removal with the V2 evaluator active; the V2 override should be a no-op

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) which is a get-or-create, persistently creating the 'Clients' type resource in the store on denied permission checks (a write side-effect on a read/authorization path); should use a read-only lookup

getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation per resource inside the resourceStore.findByType callback, making listing clients O(n·evaluations) over all client resources — expensive on hot admin-list paths
New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope (and canMapClientScopeRoles) has no test coverage; testMapRolesAndCompositeOnlyOneClient only exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE
getEvaluationContext(...) is dead code (never called) along with the unused static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE; remove it or wire it up

Three nearly identical private permission-evaluation loops (hasPermission(client, scope), hasPermission(scope), hasGrantedPermission) duplicate the scope-matching logic, and Arrays.asList(scope) is rebuilt inside/around the loop for each permission checked; extract a shared helper and pass the scope string directly

testManageAllClients discards the create response without asserting status (realmAdminClient...clients().create(newClient).close()), so a 403/400 failure surfaces later as a confusing hasSize(1) assertion error instead of at the create call

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on ClientRemovedEvent when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, so deleting a client (and roles/groups via the same listener path) will throw and abort removal with the V2 evaluator active; the V2 override should be a no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled it handles `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` (and similarly for groups/roles). This diff introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, where `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` is overridden to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If the V2 permissions implementation is active for `management(...)`, the listener will throw during client removal handling, potentially breaking cleanup/removal flow. A no-op (or supported implementation) is needed to avoid exceptions on removal events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) fallback calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) which is a get-or-create, persistently creating the 'Clients' type resource in the store on denied permission checks (a write side-effect on a read/authorization path); should use a read-only lookup

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel,String), there is a fallback to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) when no per-client resource exists. However, the diff does not show the implementation of getResourceTypeResource (it lives in AuthorizationSchema / elsewhere), so the claim that it is a get-or-create that persistently writes a 'Clients' type resource on denied checks is not verifiable from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission runs a full policy evaluation per resource inside the resourceStore.findByType callback, making listing clients O(n·evaluations) over all client resources — expensive on hot admin-list paths

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the code iterates all client resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, resource -> { ... })` and for each resource calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`, which invokes `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server)`. This performs a full permission evaluation per resource, making the operation O(number_of_client_resources × evaluation_cost). That’s a concrete performance concern introduced by this diff, but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope (and canMapClientScopeRoles) has no test coverage; testMapRolesAndCompositeOnlyOneClient only exercises MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into the `CLIENTS` resource type scopes set, plus adds `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` which checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the added/updated tests, `PermissionClientTest.testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` only grants `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (and `CONFIGURE`) for the client and never grants or exercises `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, and no other test in the shown diff appears to cover this new scope/method. This is a concrete missing-test-coverage issue for newly added authorization logic, not a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Three nearly identical private permission-evaluation loops (hasPermission(client, scope), hasPermission(scope), hasGrantedPermission) duplicate the scope-matching logic, and Arrays.asList(scope) is rebuilt inside/around the loop for each permission checked; extract a shared helper and pass the scope string directly

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, there is duplicated scope-checking/evaluation logic across `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String)`, each iterating over `Collection<Permission>` and scanning `permission.getScopes()` for a match. This is a maintainability/performance refactor opportunity (e.g., a shared helper and direct `scope.equals(s)` matching). However, the finding’s claim that `Arrays.asList(scope)` is rebuilt “for each permission checked” is slightly overstated: `expectedScopes` is created once per method call (outside the loops), not per-iteration, though it’s still unnecessary overhead compared to direct string comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testManageAllClients discards the create response without asserting status (realmAdminClient...clients().create(newClient).close()), so a 403/400 failure surfaces later as a confusing hasSize(1) assertion error instead of at the create call

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testManageAllClients, after granting the permission it does `realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(newClient).close();` and then asserts the client exists via `findByClientId`/`hasSize(1)`. The create call’s HTTP status is not checked (unlike earlier in the same test where it uses try-with-resources and asserts FORBIDDEN), so if creation fails (e.g., still 403/400), the failure would surface later as an unrelated size assertion. This is a test-robustness/diagnostics issue rather than a functional defect in production code.
